svg.aria-label: Four Properties of a Claim a Reader Can Assess showing specificity, baseline, attribution and evidence, and the same claim rewritten to have all four
svg.title: Four Properties of a Claim a Reader Can Assess
svg.text: Four Properties of a Claim a Reader Can Assess
A reader deciding how much to believe you looks at these four, mostly without noticing they are doing it.
1. Specific — a number with a unit
"significantly faster" is a feeling
"840ms" is a fact. Adjectives that sound like measurements are the
most common failure in a portfolio.
2. Baseline — the value it came from
"reduced latency to 840ms" — from what?
It could be an improvement, a regression, or no change. A number
without a starting point is a fact about the present.
3. Attributed — what YOU did
"I" over shared work is dishonest. "We" over your own work
undersells it. Naming BOTH is strongest, and rarest, because it
takes more words and more honesty.
4. Evidenced — a link a stranger can open
localhost:8080 is evidence to you and nobody else
Decidable from the string alone, so the check needs no network.
All four, in one sentence:
I cut p95 answer latency from 4.2s to 840ms by adding an IVF index, while the team migrated ingestion.
Longer than "blazing performance", and not padded — every extra word is a fact the reader can use: what changed,
from what to what, by what mechanism, and who did it. The first asks to be believed; this one offers to be checked.
